newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch museum discovers two Mondriaan oils.
newsitem.headline: Dutch museum discovers two Mondriaan oils.

text.p: Two previously unknown oil paintings by Dutch artist Piet Mondriaan have been discovered at the painter's birthplace, the Mondriaanhuis Museum said on Friday, the 125th anniversary of his birth.

The two oils on canvas, one bearing Mondriaan's signature, were authenticated by Robert Walsh, a professor of art history specialising in Mondriaan's early work, according to a statement from the museum in Amersfoort in the central Netherlands.

The discovery of "Landscape with Trees" (1900-1905) and "Portrait of C. Bergman" (1907) follows last November's find of other early works dating from when Mondriaan was still painting landscapes and portraits.
Mondriaan produced his more famous works during his later "Stijl" period, composing large canvases mostly of squares and lines in primary colors.
